name: Discover Unowned and Stale Team Tasks
prompt:
The team_workspace/ folder on the desktop contains our team's work materials from the past 3 months: meeting transcripts (meeting_transcripts/), chat records (slack_export/), task-system export (jira_export.csv), and project documents (project_docs/).
Help me find out: what things is the team currently pushing forward but with no clear owner in practice?
Please scan the action items from all sources, for example: a meeting says “let's confirm this plan next week” but no task was created; or a task does have an owner, but the owner says in chat that they thought someone else was responsible for it.
Finally, organize the results into three categories:
1. unowned tasks (clear work content but no owner);
2. ambiguous ownership (different sources contradict each other on who is responsible);
3. stale tasks (the task exists but has made no progress for a long time and the related discussion has stopped).
Output to /root/Desktop/team_workspace/unowned_analysis.md.
Further requirement: for high-confidence items (consistent information and sufficient evidence), directly fill in the owner field in jira_export.csv and save it as a new file jira_export_updated.csv; for low-confidence items, do not make changes on your own — organize them into a “to-be-confirmed list” appended to the end of the report, stating who needs to be asked to confirm what.

note: Finding work that “no one is responsible for”. The agent is given: a company team's meeting transcripts from the past 3 months + Slack/chat documents + Jira/task documents + project docs. The user says: “Help me find out what things the team is currently pushing forward but with no clear owner in practice.” The agent needs to: search across meetings, tasks, and chats for all kinds of action items; for example, a meeting says “let's confirm this plan next week” but no task was created; or a task does have an owner, but the owner says in chat that they thought someone else was responsible. Finally, generate the three categories unowned tasks / ambiguous ownership / stale tasks and give recommendations. Further requirement: for high-confidence items, directly create tasks; for low-confidence items, do not act on your own but organize them into a to-be-confirmed list. Difficulty: “owner” is implicit information, and different sources may contradict each other; this tests implicit state reconstruction + uncertainty calibration + selective action.
env_description: team_workspace/: meeting_transcripts/ (3 meetings, with unowned action items planted), slack_export/ (owner buck-passing and a departed original owner planted), jira_export.csv (10 records, including types such as empty assignee, long-term stagnation, and owner unaware), project_docs/ (the Q4 goals document notes that the owner for gray-release traffic switching is to be determined); high- and low-confidence items are mixed to test selective execution.
